fields.name: Date Palm
fields.about: A tall desert palm (Phoenix dactylifera) that has been grown across Arabia for thousands of years. It tolerates heat and drought and can live for over 100 years.
fields.used_for: Its sweet fruit (dates) is eaten fresh or dried. Leaves are woven into baskets and mats, and the trunk is used for building.

fields.name: Olive Tree
fields.about: An evergreen Mediterranean tree (Olea europaea) with silvery-green leaves and a twisted trunk. Very long-lived and drought tolerant.
fields.used_for: Olives are cured and eaten, and pressed to make olive oil. The wood is used for carving and utensils.

fields.name: Neem Tree
fields.about: A fast-growing evergreen tree (Azadirachta indica) native to the Indian subcontinent, widely planted for shade in hot climates.
fields.used_for: Used for shade and as a windbreak. Neem oil from its seeds is used as a natural insect repellent and in soaps.

fields.name: Mango
fields.about: A tropical tree (Mangifera indica) that produces large, juicy stone fruits with orange flesh. Grown in Jazan in southern Saudi Arabia.
fields.used_for: The fruit is eaten fresh, in juices, smoothies, and desserts. Unripe mangoes are used in pickles and chutneys.

fields.name: Pomegranate
fields.about: A small deciduous tree (Punica granatum) whose round fruit is packed with juicy red seeds called arils. Grown in Taif and Al Baha.
fields.used_for: The seeds are eaten fresh, added to salads, or pressed into juice and molasses.

fields.name: Watermelon
fields.about: A vining plant (Citrullus lanatus) that produces large fruits with sweet, red, water-rich flesh. Thrives in hot, sunny weather.
fields.used_for: Eaten fresh as a refreshing summer fruit and used in juices. The seeds can be roasted as a snack.

fields.name: Tomato
fields.about: A plant (Solanum lycopersicum) that produces red, juicy fruits. Botanically a fruit, but used in cooking as a vegetable.
fields.used_for: Used in salads, sauces, soups, and stews. One of the most used ingredients in kitchens worldwide.

fields.name: Carrot
fields.about: A root vegetable (Daucus carota) with a crunchy orange taproot and feathery green leaves.
fields.used_for: Eaten raw as a snack or in salads, cooked in soups and stews, and juiced. Rich in beta-carotene.

fields.name: Mint
fields.about: A fast-spreading aromatic herb (Mentha) with fresh-smelling green leaves. Easy to grow in pots.
fields.used_for: Added to tea, especially Arabic tea, and used in salads, drinks, and sauces.

fields.name: Basil
fields.about: A fragrant herb (Ocimum basilicum) with soft, bright green leaves. It loves warmth and sunlight.
fields.used_for: Used in pesto, pasta, pizza, and salads. Also used to flavour drinks and teas.

fields.name: Taif Rose
fields.about: A highly fragrant pink damask rose (Rosa x damascena) grown in the mountains of Taif, famous for its scent.
fields.used_for: Distilled into rose water and rose oil for perfumes. Rose water is also used to flavour desserts and drinks.

fields.name: Moth Orchid
fields.about: A popular indoor orchid (Phalaenopsis) with long-lasting flowers shaped like moths. Prefers bright, indirect light.
fields.used_for: Grown as a decorative houseplant and given as a gift. Its flowers can last for several months.

fields.name: Jade Plant
fields.about: A succulent (Crassula ovata) with thick, shiny, coin-shaped leaves. Stores water in its leaves and needs little care.
fields.used_for: Grown as an indoor decorative plant and bonsai. Toxic to cats and dogs, so keep it away from pets.

fields.name: Snake Plant
fields.about: A hardy plant (Dracaena trifasciata) with tall, stiff, upright leaves. Survives low light and irregular watering.
fields.used_for: A popular low-maintenance houseplant for homes and offices. Toxic if eaten by pets.
